transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi… um, I came in because I’ve been getting really frustrated with myself lately. It’s mostly these small everyday things that I normally should be able to keep track of, but I keep forgetting them.

Like, I’ll mean to return a phone call and then realize later that I never did it, or I’ll have a registration form that needs to be turned in and it just sits there because I completely lose track of it. Or I’ll be driving home and I’m supposed to stop for one simple errand, and then I get home and remember I never stopped.

It sounds minor when I say it out loud, but it’s been happening enough that I finally thought, okay, maybe I should talk to someone instead of just being annoyed with myself all the time.
Do you find yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, especially in relation to these frustrations with yourself?

I don’t know that I’d say hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get upset with myself, definitely. It’s more like embarrassment or irritation, like, “Why can’t I just do the simple thing?” And then I’ll kind of replay it in my head longer than I probably need to.

But losing interest in things… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that as the main issue. I still want to do things I enjoy, at least I think I do. It’s more that when I mess something up or forget something, I feel discouraged for a while, and then I try to move on. So… I don’t think it’s like I’m walking around feeling hopeless all the time. It’s more frustration with myself than anything.

Have you noticed these kinds of forgetfulness or disorganization in other areas of your life, like at work, in conversations, or when following through on responsibilities, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Yes, I think so. I mean, it’s not like everything is falling apart, but it shows up in these ordinary responsibilities that I really should be able to just handle. That’s actually what finally made me come in.

Like I’ll have a call I’m supposed to return, and I’ll fully intend to do it, sometimes I’ll even think about what I’m going to say, and then somehow the day goes on and I realize I never called back. Or there was a registration form I needed to turn in, and it wasn’t complicated or anything, it just… sat there. I kept meaning to do it, and then it would disappear from my mind again.

And the errands thing is embarrassing too, because I’ll be driving home and I’ll know I need to stop somewhere for one simple thing, and then I’ll pull into my driveway and remember, oh, I never stopped. It’s those kinds of little daily things. They sound small, but when they keep happening, it makes me feel like I can’t trust myself to follow through even when I’m trying.

Can you describe how you manage tasks that require sustained attention, like completing a project at work or following a detailed conversation? Do you find yourself easily distracted or struggling to stay focused on what needs to be done?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I try to stay on task, especially at work, because I know I need to get things done, but it doesn’t take much to pull me away from what I’m doing.

Like at the office, if I’m working on something and a phone rings nearby, even if it’s not my phone, my attention just goes there. Or if people are talking somewhere close by, I’ll start catching bits of what they’re saying, and then I realize I’ve stopped focusing on the thing in front of me. Sometimes it isn’t even something happening around me — I’ll just have a random thought about something at home, like something I need to do later, and suddenly I’m not really with the task anymore.

It’s frustrating because it’s not like I’m trying to ignore my work. I’ll sit there and tell myself, okay, just finish this one thing, but then something small interrupts my focus, and it takes me a while to get back to where I was. And by then I might have lost my place or forgotten what part I was on, so I kind of have to reorient myself again.
Have you experienced these same kinds of attention and focus problems since childhood, or do they seem to be more recent issues that started in adulthood?

No, I don’t think it’s totally new. I mean, it feels more noticeable now because I’m an adult and I’m supposed to keep track of everything myself, but when I think back, there were definitely versions of this when I was a kid.

Even in elementary school, I was kind of that kid who would forget the permission slip at home, or it would be in my backpack but I wouldn’t turn it in. Or I’d do homework and then somehow lose it in the mess of my backpack, so it looked like I hadn’t done it. I remember my mom having to remind me over and over, like step by step, to finish projects or get things packed up. And teachers would do that too sometimes, like breaking things down for me or reminding me what I was supposed to be doing next.

At the time I don’t think anyone made a huge thing out of it, and I guess I didn’t either. I was just seen as forgetful or needing extra reminders. But looking back now, it does feel like the same pattern, just in a kid version.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying still, especially in situations where you’re expected to remain seated or calm?

Yeah, somewhat. I wouldn’t say I’m constantly pacing or anything like that, but in situations where I’m supposed to sit still for a long time, I definitely notice it.

Like during longer classes or trainings, I’ll catch myself clicking my pen over and over, or bouncing my foot under the desk, or shifting around in the chair because I feel like I can’t quite get comfortable. And the thing is, I’m usually trying to pay attention, so it’s not like I’m doing it on purpose to be annoying or because I don’t care. Sometimes I don’t even realize I’m doing it until I hear the pen clicking or notice my leg going.

It’s kind of embarrassing if I think other people can see it, so I’ll try to stop, but then a few minutes later I’m doing something else, like changing positions or tapping my foot again. It’s not severe, I guess, but it is there, especially when I’m expected to just sit quietly and stay focused for a while.
